record.title: CS/CS/SB 1798 (2022): Sexually Related Offenses
record.short_title: Florida SB 1798 (2022): altered sexual depictions offence
record.issuing_body: Florida Legislature (2022 Regular Session; sponsors Appropriations and Criminal Justice Committees and Sen. Book); approved by the Governor
record.official_identifier: Laws of Florida ch. 2022-212 (CS/CS/SB 1798, 2022); creates ss. 836.13 and 836.14, F.S.
record.summary: Creates s. 836.13, F.S., an offence for sexual deepfakes: willfully and maliciously promoting an altered sexual depiction of an identifiable person without consent, knowing or having reason to know it is altered, is a third-degree felony, and victims have a civil action. An altered sexual depiction is a realistic depiction of an identifiable person, produced by any digital or other modification, with another person's or computer-generated nude body parts or engaged in sexual conduct the person did not engage in; a disclaimer is no defence. The act also extends child pornography to images created or modified to portray an identifiable minor and criminalises theft of sexually explicit images.
record.notes: Passed the Senate 37-0 on 3 Mar 2022 and the House 117-0 on 8 Mar 2022; approved by the Governor on 24 Jun 2022 and effective 1 Oct 2022. Victims of an altered sexual depiction may seek injunctive relief, damages of USD 10,000 or actual damages, whichever is greater, and attorney fees; providers of interactive computer, information or communications services, law enforcement, people reporting unlawful activity and participants in legal proceedings are exempt. Section 836.14 makes theft of a sexually explicit image with intent to promote it, and possessing a stolen image with intent to promote it for financial gain, third-degree felonies, and promoting such an image for financial gain without consent a second-degree felony. The act also amends the definitions of child pornography in ss. 775.0847 and 827.071 to cover images created, altered, adapted or modified by electronic, mechanical or other means to portray an identifiable minor, raises damages for sexual cyberharassment and increases penalties for sexual activities involving animals. Section 836.13 was amended by ch. 2025-99 (CS/CS/HB 757), which added offences for generating, soliciting and possessing altered sexual depictions, by ch. 2025-133 (CS/CS/HB 1161, Brooke's Law), which added platform removal duties, and in 2026 by ch. 2026-14, ch. 2026-18 and ch. 2026-20.
record.scope_note: Not an AI-specific law: a broad sexual offences act. Included because it created Florida's offence for promoting sexual deepfakes (altered sexual depictions, including computer-generated nude body parts), the statute that later Florida deepfake laws extend.

verification.note: Stored the Florida Senate bill page for SB 1798 (2022), the Senate Criminal Justice Committee analyses of January 2022, the enrolled text of CS/CS/SB 1798 (20221798er, 62 pages) and the 2026 Florida Statutes page for s. 836.13 (all flsenate.gov). The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, history, floor votes (37-0 and 117-0), approval by the Governor on 24 Jun 2022, Chapter No. 2022-212 and the 1 Oct 2022 effective date; the enrolled text confirms every provision in the summary and notes (sections 1, 3, 5 and 6) and the effective-date clause (section 13); the statute page shows s. 836.13 in force in the 2026 edition with a history note citing ch. 2025-99, ch. 2025-133, ch. 2026-14, ch. 2026-18 and ch. 2026-20. The statute page gives no amendment dates, so date_last_updated is the year 2026. The Criminal Justice analyses describe an earlier version (for example renaming child pornography as child sexual abuse material, which the enacted act does not do) and were not used for the summary.

judgment.status_reasoning: Approved by the Governor on 24 Jun 2022 (Chapter No. 2022-212); section 13 of the enrolled act: 'This act shall take effect October 1, 2022.' That date is before today (14 Oct 2026), so in force. Section 836.13 appears in the 2026 Florida Statutes with a history note listing later amendments and no repeal.
judgment.scope_reasoning: Borderline, included with a scope_note under the rule for laws that are not AI-specific but are the operative instrument for an AI-safety question (deepfakes): a broad sexual offences act whose s. 836.13 is Florida's base offence for sexual deepfakes, which the staff analysis describes as 'Colloquially known as "deep fakes"'.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's approval (24 Jun 2022); date_in_force the effective-date clause (1 Oct 2022). date_last_updated is '2026': the stored statute page shows amendments of s. 836.13 by three 2026 session laws (ch. 2026-14, ch. 2026-18, ch. 2026-20) but gives no dates, so the year is the precision the stored files support.
judgment.related_reasoning: C005 (CS/CS/HB 757, 2025, ch. 2025-99) and C004 (CS/CS/HB 1161, Brooke's Law, 2025, ch. 2025-133) both amend s. 836.13, which this act created; the stored statute page cites s. 3, ch. 2025-99 and s. 2, ch. 2025-133.
judgment.summary_reasoning: Written from the enrolled text: s. 836.13(1)(a), (2), (4) and (5) (section 5), the child pornography definitions in ss. 775.0847(1) and 827.071(1) (sections 1 and 3), and s. 836.14 (section 6).
judgment.topics_reasoning: deepfakes & synthetic media and accountability & liability for s. 836.13 and its civil action; child safety for the extension of child pornography to images modified to portray an identifiable minor.
